newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-NEWCASTLE LET TWO-GOAL LEAD SLIP AT VILLA.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-NEWCASTLE LET TWO-GOAL LEAD SLIP AT VILLA.

text.p: Newcastle ended one of the most traumatic weeks in their recent history by squandering a two-goal lead and drawing 2-2 with Aston Villa in the English premier league on Saturday.

Playing their first match since the shock resignation of manager Kevin Keegan on Wednesday, Newcastle raced into a 2-0 lead in what turned out to be a thrilling match with goals from Alan Shearer (16th) and Lee Clark (21st).
But Villa fought back with goals from Dwight Yorke (39th) and Savo Milosevic (52nd). Yorke also had a poorly taken penalty saved by goalkeeper Shaka Hislop after 61 minutes.
There was no change at the top with leaders Liverpool being held to a 0-0 draw at home by West Ham and second-placed Arsenal having a nightmare against Sunderland.
They lost 1-0 with their Dutch striker Dennis Bergkamp sent off after 29 minutes and skipper Tony Adams putting through his own goal in the 66th.
Third-placed Manchester United play Tottenham on Sunday.

Blackburn ended Coventry's recent revival and continued their own with a 4-0 win at Ewood Park, their biggest win of the season and the biggest of the day. Coventry's Dion Dublin was sent off for the second successive match.
